subtopics.title: Why Two Records of One Bank Account Differ

questions.question: An outstanding deposit is best described as:
options: A TIMING difference — correctly recorded by the business, not yet cleared by the bank
An omission by the business that must be journalised
An error by the bank
A dishonoured receipt

questions.question: Bank charges, interest credited, stop orders and debit orders appear first on the bank statement because:
options: The bank makes them up
The business did not initiate them and was not told, so they were never journalised
They are always errors
They belong on the reconciliation statement only

questions.question: The governing rule of the topic is that:
options: Everything on the statement is entered in the journals
Nothing on the statement is entered in the journals
Our omissions and our errors are corrected in our books; timing differences and the bank's errors go on the reconciliation statement
Only amounts over R1 000 are corrected

questions.question: Before touching any figure in a bank reconciliation question, each item must first be:
options: Converted to a percentage
Added to the bank statement
Posted to the general ledger
Placed in one of three boxes — timing difference, our omission, or error

questions.question: A debtor's EFT of R6 800, already recorded in the CRJ, is dishonoured. The correcting entry is:
options: Debit Debtors control, credit Bank
Debit Bad debts, credit Bank
Debit Bank, credit Debtors control
Debit Bank charges, credit Bank

questions.question: A payment to a creditor of R4 380 was entered in the CPJ as R3 480. The correction is:
options: Debit Bank R900, credit Creditors control R900
Debit Creditors control R900, credit Bank R900
Debit Creditors control R4 380, credit Bank R4 380
No correction — the bank is wrong

questions.question: Cheque 1046 for R9 300, issued on 20 August 2025 and still unpresented at 28 February 2026, must be:
options: Left on the outstanding list indefinitely
Written off as a bad debt
Cancelled as stale — debit Bank, credit Creditors control
Added to the bank statement balance

questions.question: Starting from a provisional Bank account balance of R64 310 and processing the seven February findings, the corrected balance is:
In the reconciliation statement, R3 700 debited to the business in error by the bank is:
options: ADDED to the bank statement balance, because the bank will give it back
Subtracted from the bank statement balance
Entered in the Cash Payments Journal
Ignored entirely

questions.question: Outstanding EFTs of R14 250 and R12 700 are treated as:
options: An addition of R26 950 to the statement balance
A deduction of R26 950 from the statement balance, because the bank still has to take them off
A correction in the Cash Receipts Journal
A stale-cheque cancellation

questions.question: The bank statement closes at R55 650. Adding the R28 400 outstanding deposit and the R3 700 bank error, and deducting R26 950 of outstanding EFTs, gives:
The reliable test for whether an item is added or subtracted on the reconciliation statement is:
options: Deposits are always added and payments always subtracted
Larger amounts are added
Follow the order on the bank statement
Ask what the BANK will still do to this balance, then follow it

subtopics.title: Traps, Method Marks and Internal Control

questions.question: Entering an outstanding deposit in the Cash Receipts Journal is wrong because:
options: It is already in our books — that is exactly why it is outstanding — so it would be recorded twice
Deposits are never journalised
The bank has already recorded it
It belongs in the Cash Payments Journal

questions.question: Method marks in this topic are protected mainly by:
options: Writing only the final balance
Showing the corrected Bank account with contra accounts named, and a fully headed reconciliation statement with brackets on every subtraction
Rounding all figures to the nearest thousand
Copying the bank statement exactly

questions.question: The internal control argument for the bank reconciliation is that:
options: It reduces bank charges
It is required by the bank
An outside party independently records every movement of cash, so comparing records catches theft, omission and error
It replaces the need for a cashier

questions.question: Deposits that repeatedly appear only after month end are the classic signature of:
options: A stale cheque
A bank error
Capitalised interest
Lapping — using a later receipt to cover an earlier theft

subtopics.title: Two People Counting the Same Money

questions.question: The stokvel comparison shows that two honest records differ mainly because:
options: Two people wrote at two different moments — same money, two clocks
One person is stealing
The bank charges fees
Money was never deposited

questions.question: The bank statement is described as "a letter from the bank" because it lists:
options: Only the mistakes you made
Everything the bank did to your money that you did not know about
Next month's projected balance
The creditors you still owe

questions.question: A customer's transfer that bounces means:
options: The bank owes you the money
The amount becomes an expense
You were never actually paid — the customer goes straight back onto the debtors list
The sale must be cancelled

subtopics.title: The Bank's News and Your Own Mistakes

questions.question: Which pile does the R28 400 uncleared deposit belong to?
options: Things you leave alone — your book is right, the bank is simply behind
News to write into the journals
Your own slip to fix
A bank fee

questions.question: A difference that divides neatly by nine usually means:
options: A missing deposit
Two digits have been swapped around — a transposition
The bank charged interest
A cheque has gone stale

questions.question: The "milk" comparison in the lesson refers to:
options: Interest accruing monthly
Bank charges rising each year
A cheque going off after six months, so it must be cancelled and the supplier put back on the list
Stock spoiling on the shelf

questions.question: The three piles a learner should sort every statement item into are:
options: Debits, credits and balances
Cash, credit and contra
Assets, expenses and income
News to journalise, your own slips to fix, and things you leave alone

subtopics.title: The Bridge Between the Two Numbers

questions.question: After all news and slips are dealt with, the two numbers being bridged are:
options: The corrected Bank account of R60 800 and the bank statement balance of R55 650
The provisional R64 310 and the statement's R55 650
The deposit of R28 400 and the transfers of R26 950
The petty cash and the bank

questions.question: The one question that decides every add and subtract on the bridge is:
options: Is it a deposit or a payment?
What is the bank still going to do to this?
Is the amount large or small?
Which journal recorded it?

questions.question: Why does "deposits are always added" fail as a rule?
options: Deposits are rare
Banks do not record deposits
It breaks the moment a question hands you an overdraft or reverses the direction of the statement
Deposits are timing differences

questions.question: Good practice for a small business doing reconciliations includes:
options: Reconciling once a year
Letting the cashier reconcile the account alone
Carrying long-outstanding items forward without question
Reconciling monthly, splitting the duties, having a partner sign it, and chasing anything long outstanding
